title: Capacity fencing and KV soft-pressure tuning for sustained high-QPS microbatching
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Problem: Under sustained high QPS with mixed sequence lengths we observe intermittent GPU OOMs and severe microbatch oscillation (queues rapidly switching between empty and saturated) which increases p95 latency and reduces batching efficiency. Current admission controllers rely on slot headroom heuristics that do not account for growing KV cache footprint or fragmenting memory from transient allocations.

Proposal summary: Implement a capacity-fence mechanism and complementary KV soft-pressure signal to stabilize microbatch admission and preserve a small guaranteed GPU memory headroom for KV cache growth. The fence is a dynamic reserved memory region per GPU (expressed as a percentage of usable memory) that we do not allocate to new batches unless explicit overcommit is allowed under emergency fallback. The KV soft-pressure signal is a lightweight telemetry metric (kv_active_ratio) emitted per model-pool which represents fraction of fence consumed by pinned KV pages; admission controller uses this to: (1) bias microbatch size selection toward smaller ceilings when kv_active_ratio > threshold, and (2) apply proportional soft backoff to request acceptance rate instead of hard rejections.

This ticket covers design, implementation, experimentation, and a cautious rollout with feature flags and observability dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: Capacity-fence calculation implemented in runtime memory manager and configurable per-pool
KV soft-pressure signal emitted by KV manager (kv_active_ratio) and consumed by admission controller
Microbatch admission policy updated to use fence-aware batch ceilings and soft proportional backoff (no silent request drops in steady state)
Integration tests that simulate growing KV footprints and verify no OOM across 60s sustained QPS at target throughput
Dashboard with p50/p95 latency, batching efficiency, OOM count, kv_active_ratio and admission backoff rate
Rollout plan validated in staging with canary at 5% traffic before gradual ramp to 100%
design_notes: Capacity fence definition: fence_size = max(fence_min, min(fence_pct * usable_mem, fence_max_bytes)). Default fence_pct = 6% of usable GPU memory, fence_min = 64MB, fence_max_bytes = 2GB.

Why fence: Provides deterministic headroom for KV cache and transient allocation spikes, reducing fragmentation-driven OOMs and preventing aggressive eviction storms that reduce cache hit-rate and increase latency.

KV soft-pressure metric: kv_active_ratio = (kv_pinned_bytes_within_fence) / fence_size. Range [0.0, 1.0+]. Emit as gauge every 250ms per model-pool and expose to admission controller with short exponential smoothing (alpha=0.2).

Admission logic: when kv_active_ratio < 0.6 -> normal batch ceilings; between 0.6-0.85 -> reduce target microbatch ceiling by linear factor (ceil = ceil * (1 - 0.4*(kv_active_ratio-0.6)/0.25)); above 0.85 -> enable proportional soft backoff based on (kv_active_ratio-0.85), capped at 50% reduction in acceptance rate. Hard rejects only if gpu_free_mem < oom_safe_threshold (emergency).
Hysteresis: use separate enter/exit thresholds for soft-pressure to avoid oscillation: enter_soft = 0.6, exit_soft = 0.5; enter_backoff = 0.85, exit_backoff = 0.8.
Per-model tuning: allow per-model overrides for fence_pct and backoff caps based on historical kv footprint profiles. Default applies to model-pools without override.
Telemetry: track batch_size_distribution, batching_efficiency (tokens_per_second / theoretical_max), admission_backoff_fraction, OOMs, evictions_per_minute, kv_hit_rate, and kv_active_ratio.
Compatibility: ensure feature disabled by default; runtime flag allow_fence=true and remote-config gating for gradual enablement.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (runtime): add fence bookkeeping to gpu_memory_manager, implement config knobs (fence_pct, fence_min, fence_max) and unit tests for boundary behavior
Phase 2 (kv): export kv_pinned_bytes_within_fence from KV manager and smoothing helper; add endpoints for querying kv_active_ratio in admin API
Phase 3 (admission): integrate kv_active_ratio into admission controller decision path, implement soft proportional backoff and hysteresis logic, add feature flag checks
Phase 4 (tests): synthetic load tests in CI that create increasing KV footprints and vary seq-length distributions; staging soak for 6 hours at production-like QPS
Phase 5 (observability & alerting): Grafana panels and alert rules for kv_active_ratio > 0.85 for 30s, increased evictions, and elevated admission_backoff_fraction
Phase 6 (rollout): canary at 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with rollback playbook.
test_plan: Unit tests for fence sizing and bounds, edge cases where usable_mem changes mid-run (GPU reconfiguration)
Integration test that simulates a heavy KV write/retain workload and validates no OOM at sustained QPS (scripts in infra/tests/microbatch_fence)
Chaos scenario: artificially reduce usable GPU memory to assert emergency fallback behaves (hard rejects only when necessary)
A/B experiment in staging comparing baseline admission controller vs fence+soft-pressure for p95 latency and batching efficiency
Load test matrix: (QPS 10k, 20k, 40k) x (avg_seq 64, 256, 1024) x (kv_growth fast/slow)
rollout: Enable feature flag for a single model-pool in staging and run a 6-hour soak with production-like traffic
Canary in prod: route 5% of traffic for low-risk models (small avg_seq) for 24 hours, monitor metrics and errors
If stable, increase to 20% for 12 hours and run a targeted KV growth stress test
Full rollout only after verified reduction in OOMs or batch oscillation without unacceptable throughput loss (p95 increase <= 10% relative)
Rollback: toggle feature flag off and immediately reduce canary to 0% if OOM or p95 regressions exceed thresholds
metrics: batching_efficiency (tokens/sec achieved / theoretical tokens/sec) per GPU
throughput (requests/sec) before and after feature toggle
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: overly-conservative fence reduces batch sizes and hurts throughput. Mitigation: start with small fence_pct default (6%) and monitor batching_efficiency; allow per-model overrides and quick rollback.
Risk: hysteresis parameters might be mis-tuned for bursty traffic causing delayed recovery. Mitigation: include smoothing alpha and separate enter/exit thresholds; run post-deploy tuning experiments.

Risk: additional metric emission increases pressure on control plane. Mitigation: kv_active_ratio emitted at 250ms but aggregated/trimmed in control plane; sample at coarser intervals for low-priority pools.

Risk: conflicting with existing eviction heuristics. Mitigation: coordinate with KV team (owners indicated in links) and add a compatibility flag to gradually turn off old heuristics when fence is stable.
